study.question: Does correctly assigning auxiliary product-context gradients to examples explain their click-AUC benefit under the common aggregate FP64 collection graph, and does retaining the occupied-row mean modify that dependence?
study.hypothesis: The latest full (0.6683663357340763) and centered (0.6682972490126902) transfer exceed blocked (0.6678548720585206), while mean-only (0.667713177167141) does not. Useful supervision may reside chiefly in example-associated variation of auxiliary context gradients. If so, a norm/sum-preserving paired permutation should reduce click AUC for both full and centered transfer. Earlier task-edge assignment contrasts were suggestive, but algebraically equivalent centered implementations and local accumulation precision changed outcomes; therefore they do not establish the mechanism for the collected FP64 model.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary v4 section4.3 lines250-277 describes target-dependent unnormalized local activation, inherited in adapted compressed form. This study changes training-only auxiliary product-context VJPs; it does not propose DIN or reproduce its original benchmark.

Primary benchmark section2.3 describes forward feature/history/task interaction including INFNet, SSR and HiFormer. We hold the inherited forward network fixed and investigate label-driven backward transfer. This source is primary for benchmark descriptions, not an original-paper audit of those methods.

Exact available source/config/hash checked. Inherit full/centered FP64 component collector; add only a common paired row-assignment operation after reduction and before casting. Earlier g3-r0037-centered_swapped and g3-r0037-full_swapped used a different task-edge accumulation topology. This is a precision-controlled follow-up, not an unverified new method claim.

study.proposed_difference: Cross component {full G, centered C=G-M} with assignment {aligned, half_swap} in one common three-output auxiliary collector. G is summed in fixed task order in FP64 over occupied histories. Eligible i iff both i and its B/2 partner have nonempty history; P swaps only these pairs and fixes other rows. Return G, P(G), C or P(C), with no renormalization. Since P preserves occupancy and M, P(G)=P(C)+M mathematically; full is computed directly from G to avoid C+M cancellation. Every arm computes the swap, selecting its returned tensor before the single inherited dtype cast. This is an explicit surrogate VJP, not the true derivative of identity forward or a new scalar objective. No task loss or inference operation changes.
predictions: Aligned centered and full arms should bridge their g3-r0042 endpoints at the same seed; this checks execution integrity and is not new repetition evidence. Any endpoint discrepancy must be resolved before attributing the new contrast.

Primary directional predictions: AUC(centered_aligned64)>AUC(centered_swapped64) and AUC(full_aligned64)>AUC(full_swapped64). Correct association would be locally supported if both contrasts survive preflight and later authorized paired repetitions.

Predeclare interaction D=[AUC(full_aligned64)-AUC(full_swapped64)]-[AUC(centered_aligned64)-AUC(centered_swapped64)]. Its sign is not predicted. A reproducible nonzero D would motivate a separate mean-by-assignment mechanism study; one-seed D remains exploratory.
No parameter or inference graph change: expect 32192421 parameters (31793216 embedding, 399205 dense) and comparable inference throughput/latency. Measure rather than infer any cost equality.
falsifiers: If centered or full swapped assignment matches or exceeds its aligned counterpart after valid execution and repetition, correct example assignment is not established as necessary for that component. If both contrasts fail, reject the proposed common assignment explanation in this setting.

If aligned replays fail to match their archived endpoints or private gradients/forward outputs differ at fixed state across assignment arms, the planned isolation fails; retain charged receipts and diagnose before mechanism claims.

A centered advantage over blocked alone, or degraded performance under swapping alone, does not establish reduced gradient interference or prove informative auxiliary supervision; shuffled-label and blocked historical controls remain complementary, not new matched FP64 causal controls.
AUC gains without repeatable comparisons to click-only, blocked and the incumbent do not establish a better final model; no holdout result is available.
alternative_explanations: One frozen seed; replays are implementation controls, not independent replication; repeated adaptive validation selection limits generalization
Pair swap preserves row-space norms/sums only. Repeated feature IDs and sparse embedding scatter change parameter-space gradients and Adagrad state
Half-batch pairs need not be independent or different users. Unswappable occupied rows remain aligned; swap is a partial association disruption
Auxiliary Dice/batch normalization couples examples; downstream training trajectories and private-task gradients diverge after the first changed update
FP64 applies only to local task reduction; upstream bf16/FP32 and downstream sparse arithmetic remain inherited
The full-minus-centered AUC difference of about 0.0000691 may reflect rounding/optimization trajectory or seed sensitivity, rather than beneficial global mean transfer.
Permuting gradients can hurt through repeated-ID scatter geometry or optimizer dynamics even without useful per-example supervision. Preserved row norms do not remove that explanation.
Historical batch-rolled-label and single-task/subset controls are negative trajectories under their own graphs; they are not exact controls for this new collector.
